hotContext.criticalNews: Samsung completed foundry-side AI5 tape-out for Taylor 2nm production (July 13). TSMC AI5 version already ahead. Volume production still H2 2027; vehicle deployment 2028+.

recentKeyChanges.title: Samsung Completes AI5 Foundry Tape-Out for Taylor 2nm; Mass Production Still 2027
recentKeyChanges.description: A Samsung Foundry principal engineer (James Kim) disclosed on LinkedIn that the Tesla-Samsung AI5 chip has reached foundry tape-out and is scheduled for manufacturing at Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab on Samsung's 2nm process. Yonhap, ET News, TrendForce, Tom's Hardware, and Electrek all covered the disclosure (the LinkedIn post was later deleted). This is a foundry-side tape-out — distinct from Tesla's April 2026 design tape-out that Musk announced — and is the first concrete Samsung production timeline public detail for AI5. Key new details: (1) AI5 will run on 2nm at Taylor, not a more mature node as previously assumed (2nm was expected for AI6); (2) AI5 volume is split between Samsung and TSMC, with TSMC's AI5 version having taped out months earlier; (3) Samsung will fully handle AI6 while TSMC handles AI6.5; (4) Taylor targets initial operations late 2026 and volume production in H2 2027. Critical reality check: tape-out is not production. Musk has said Tesla needs several hundred thousand completed AI5 boards before vehicle line switchover — still expected mid-to-late 2027. AI5 remains nearly two years behind original timelines, Cybercab launches on AI4, and Samsung Foundry continues operating at a loss (~KRW 600B estimated in non-memory for Q2).

positive_signals: Samsung foundry-side AI5 tape-out completed — design locked for Taylor 2nm manufacturing
AI5 confirmed dual-sourced: Samsung (Taylor 2nm) + TSMC (version taped out months earlier)
Putting AI5 on 2nm (not just AI6) signals Samsung 2nm yield may have crossed viability threshold (~60% assumed)
Taylor fab equipment move-in since April 2026; initial ops targeted late 2026, volume H2 2027
AI6 exclusive to Samsung under $16.5B deal; AI6.5 assigned to TSMC — clearer supply allocation
Korean engineering samples (KR 2613 marking) already demonstrated by Musk in May 2026
negative_signals: Tape-out is NOT production — engineering samples and qualification still required before mass production
High-volume AI5 still mid-to-late 2027; vehicles won't get meaningful AI5 until 2028 at earliest
AI5 nearly 2 years behind original schedule; Cybercab still launching on outdated AI4 hardware
TSMC AI5 version taped out months ahead of Samsung — Samsung remains the lagging foundry partner
Samsung Foundry still loss-making (~KRW 600B non-memory operating loss estimated Q2 2026); recovery depends on unproven 2nm yields at Taylor
No confirmed yield data published; 2nm process risk remains the gating item for both AI5 volume and AI6 (already slipped to mid-2028)
LinkedIn disclosure was unofficial and deleted — not a formal Samsung or Tesla production announcement
